title: The picks page accounted for 23 of the 33 matches it said carried a pick (fixed on main by 4c972a51; regression test added here)
detail: Read on the live site at 2026-10-22T07:47Z, /picks/ printed: '33 of 33 matches below carry a pick. 11 come from an external market, esportsbook or aggregated bookmaker line, 12 more from the audited research ladder, badged Researched fallback, and 0 remain blank because no supported evidence exists.' 11 + 12 = 23, so ten rows were unaccounted for. The cause was arithmetic, not data: the first number came from data['counts'] (featured-method rows only) while the page renders the effective basis (featured pick, otherwise an audited fallback), and the second number counted fallbacks. The executive summary on the same snapshot printed the correct split (15 external line, 18 research model, 0 unresolved), so the two pages disagreed. Two sessions diagnosed and fixed this independently: 4c972a51's implementation landed on main first (it derives every number from the displayed-basis tally and adds a wide-book bucket) and is the version in the merged tree; this session's equivalent change was dropped during the merge rather than stacked on top of it. What this session contributes on top is the regression test: tests/test_93ba7221_counts.py reads the published numbers out of the sentence and asserts that the groups add up to the rows with a pick, that a stale counts block cannot reach it, and that the executive summary and the picks page agree.

title: The coverage page's 'Future probabilities' card read 23 / 33 while the summary said 33 of 33 had a pick (fixed)
detail: On the same 2026-10-22T05:36Z snapshot, /coverage/ showed 'Future probabilities 23 / 33' and the executive summary showed '33 of 33 ... with a directional pick'. Both numbers were correct for different things (featured stages only versus featured plus the researched ladder) but neither was labelled, which is exactly the kind of contradiction that made the site hard to read. The merged fix, from 4c972a51, keeps the featured fraction and adds the researched list's own figure in the same card ('the researched list has N of M with a pick and Z unresolved'), so a reader can see both without arithmetic. This session's alternative labelling was dropped in the merge for the same reason. Locked by CoverageCardConsistencyTests.

title: Hotspawn added at least five fixtures in the two and a half hours after the published snapshot; they reach the site at the next refresh
detail: Read through the agent's page reader at 2026-10-22T07:51Z, Hotspawn's scheduled-fixture API contains five CCT South America 2026 Series #7 fixtures that do not exist anywhere in the published 05:36:38Z snapshot: 1082921 your end vs Yawara (22 Oct 19:00Z), 1082922 Low Cortisol BR vs Grêmio (22 Oct 22:00Z), 1082924 BORRACHEIROS vs QUINTESSÊNCIA (23 Oct 16:00Z), 1082925 BESTIA Academy vs RED Canids Academy (23 Oct 19:00Z) and 1082926 Isurus vs Hacha (23 Oct 22:00Z). The published /picks/ page lists no CCT South America tournament at all, so these cannot be duplicates of published rows. This is not a collector defect: the snapshot's own cross-check required the fixture API and every readable lobby payload to agree exactly at 05:36:38Z, and these records were not in those responses then. It measures the blind window the four-hour refresh creates, which is why the pages scope every coverage claim to 'this snapshot' and print the observation time. The refresh that follows this PR is verified against these five ids; see the session record in COORDINATION.md.

title: The CSV download answered HTTP 500 to the page reader while JSON and HTML pages answered 200 (unverified, not claimed broken)
detail: Requested at 2026-10-22T07:44Z, https://buffedlizard55-lab.github.io/MaltaProj3/data/picks.csv returned HTTP 500 to the agent's page reader, while /data/latest.json, /data/sources.json and the HTML pages on the same host returned 200. GitHub Pages serves .csv as text/csv, and the reader may simply not render that content type, so this is published as unverified rather than as a broken link. The CSV is generated by scripts/build.py picks_csv() from the same rows the HTML table renders and is covered by the repository's row-source audit, but a successful download has not been observed by this session and no claim is made that it works.

title: Verification: 12 research-model picks replay exactly from Valve's official standings file
detail: Twelve research-model picks on the published 2026-10-22T05:36Z snapshot were recomputed from Valve's official live/2026/standings_global_2026_10_05.md with the formula the methodology page documents (fixed rating deviation 75, g = 1/sqrt(1 + 3*(ln10/400)^2*75^2/pi^2), p = 1/(1+10^(g*(r_b-r_a)/400))). All twelve reproduce the published one-decimal percentage within 0.05 percentage points, which is display rounding: BakS-Azuolas 73.4%, Nemesis-WW 91.8%, Donstu-Banda chuya 59.5%, BakS-BRUTE 59.9%, ex-RUSTEC-Saint Sinners 80.7%, 6yuBoJlbl-ex-6666 62.6%, Nuclear TigeRES-ILLYRIANS 93.0%, Lynn Vision-Chinggis Warriors 64.4%, NEXVOID-Alter Ego 72.8%, Rooster-Abyssal 52.2%, 5star-1WIN 82.2% and HOTU-The Huns 94.1%. Where Valve's table holds several rows for one name, the published number is reproduced only by a complete five-player row - Banda Chuya 801 (standing 165) not the two-player 402 remnant, BRUTE 1116 (standing 75) not 689, ex-RUSTEC 1066 (standing 92) not the four-player 824 row, Chinggis Warriors 1084 (standing 87) not 685, The Huns 944 (standing 122) not 701, and ex-6666 through the reviewed alias registry to Valve's 6666 at 923 (standing 127) not the 425 four-player remnant. The money-line rows and the bo3.gg network/form rows are outside this replay and no claim is made about them here.

title: The repository's own phone check was failing before this branch: Picks at a Glance sat 26 px below the 1,500 px budget (fixed on main by df80ab9f)
detail: tests/browser/dashboard.spec.mjs asserts that #picks-at-a-glance starts above 1,500 px at 320 px and 390 px wide. Built from origin/main at 2fb99b0 (PR #167) in a clean worktree, the block started at y = 1526.25 px at 390 px wide and the check failed (83 passed, 2 failed); 75aa5b56's longer banner copy, aria-labels and 48 px tap targets are what pushed it past the budget. This session measured the failure, fixed it locally (320 px -> 1326.7 px, 390 px -> 1364.0 px, 85/85 Playwright checks green) and then found that df80ab9f had landed an equivalent compaction on main, so the merge kept main's CSS and dropped this session's duplicate block. The finding stands: the budget was red on main and is green now, and no pick, probability or source was involved.
